title: Evaluation-compatible realization of common-stage coefficients as native adic modules
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T$ be separated of finite type over $k$. Let $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$ be the finite-extension-valued coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], and write $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal C_T$ be the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], using the raw rationalizations of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $D^b_{\mathrm{cons}}(\mathcal A_T)$ for the full subcategory of $D(\mathcal A_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with bounded cohomology, each cohomology sheaf admitting a finite locally closed stratification on which it is pro-etale locally finite free over the restricted coefficient ring.

There is a canonical exact equivalence
$$\rho_T:\mathcal C_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_{\mathrm{cons}}(\mathcal A_T).$$
On $(E,M)$ it is derived scalar extension to $R_T$ of the continuous $E$-coefficient realization of an integral representative of $M$; it sends a common-stage arrow to the scalar extension of the same finite-stage arrow. Its scalar comparisons are induced by balanced tensor multiplication. The equivalence is symmetric strong monoidal and preserves the coefficient unit. Whenever $M,N$ and the coefficient-passage internal Hom $H=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$ belong to $\mathcal C_T$, its evaluation-transpose comparison
$$\rho_T H\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{R_T}(\rho_TM,\rho_TN)$$
is an isomorphism in the ambient derived category, natural in both variables and carrying the evaluation $H\otimes M\to N$ to module evaluation. The tensor and Hom on the left are precisely those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. These comparisons respect symmetry, finite coefficient-field extension and the identity and composition maps of scheme isomorphisms, including geometric Frobenius. Thus the ordinary module category here is the native adic module presentation, not a category over discrete $\Omega$.

This reuses the already packaged realization instead of repeating finite cocone and common-stage descent. All hypotheses hold because T is finite type over the fixed geometric field and the identity is separated, finite type and proper.
